title: W-2: pasted bytes left on stdin reach the shell, and the passphrase is silently truncated at 1024 bytes
description: Source: the consolidated pre-public security review (opum-doc, 2026-10-30), reviewed at b1dae53374a8c0c3514f015ff77faac9af643e2d; tracked under ODOC-552 and parent WCLI-95. Report id: W-2 (high). Both hidden readers stop at the first newline and restore echo without discarding queued input; the secret reader leaves bytes past a refusal unread and the passphrase reader truncates silently at its bound, so the confirm step compares two identically truncated values. No tcflush exists in src/. Files: src/adapters/secret-value.ts, src/adapters/passphrase.ts. One PTY test against the shipped artifact is still owed (the reviewer ran a mirror on a standalone runtime).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The passphrase reader refuses at its bound, as the secret reader does, and never truncates silently
Both readers flush pending input (tcflush TCIFLUSH) on every exit path, success, refusal and Ctrl-C, before restoring echo
A real-PTY test with a multiline paste, a refusal and a Ctrl-C shows no leftover bytes reach the shell
One PTY check is run against the packaged binary
